title: Senior Product Designer
summary: Lead engagements end to end, from first workshop to shipped product.

aboutParagraphs: You will lead engagements end to end — sitting in the first workshop, shaping the product direction, designing the interface system, and staying through build until it ships.
Most of our work is enterprise: lending platforms, fleet systems, internal tools with twelve years of accumulated logic. The interesting problem is rarely the screen. It is the model underneath it.

groups.heading: What you will do
items: Run discovery with users who are hard to reach and busier than you
Turn messy domain logic into product direction a team can act on
Design interface systems, not one-off screens — components, tokens, states
Work directly with client engineers through build, not over a handoff wall
Help shape how the studio itself works as we grow

groups.heading: What we are looking for
items: Six or more years designing digital products, some of it on complex B2B or enterprise work
A portfolio that shows systems thinking, not only polished visuals
Comfort with ambiguity — most engagements start before the problem is clearly stated
Ability to explain a design decision to an engineer, a CFO and a user in three different ways
Fluency in Figma including variables, components and auto-layout

groups.heading: Nice to have
items: Experience building or maintaining a design system used by more than one product
Front-end literacy — you do not have to ship code, but you should be able to read it
Fintech, logistics or regulated industry background

groups.heading: How we hire
items: Intro call — 30 minutes, mutual fit
Portfolio walkthrough — one project, in depth, your choice
Paid design exercise — a real problem, about four hours, we pay for your time
Team conversation — meet the people you would work with
groups.intro: Four steps, about two weeks end to end. We tell you where you stand after every one.

detail.applyBody: Send your portfolio and a short note about a system you are proud of. No cover letter needed.
